
```{r}
metaphlan_kraken_output_file<-'kraken_metaphlan_consensus_species.tsv'
crypts_file <- '../Data/crypt_signature_attributions.csv'
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
```

```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. CONFIG
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

INPUT_FILE   <- metaphlan_kraken_output_file  # your table
OUTDIR       <- "./"
ANNOT_FILE   <- "./taxon_annotation.R"  # shared blacklist/allowlist module
RANK         <- "s"      # "s" species, "g" genus, "t" SGB
READ_LEN     <- 150      # mean read length (bp)
PAIRED       <- TRUE     # TRUE if counts are read PAIRS
MIN_READS_TAXON <- 10    # reads needed to call a taxon "detected" in a sample
GUT_CATALOGUE <- NULL           # optional path to UHGG genomes-all_metadata.tsv
BLANKS        <- character(0)   # column names of true negative controls, if any
DB_N_DECOY  <- NA_real_   # reference entries in impossible clades
DB_N_TARGET <- NA_real_   # reference entries everywhere else
FDR_TARGET  <- 0.05       # report the abundance threshold achieving this FDR
CRYPT_FILE  <- crypts_file

## Pragmatic convention only, for the pass/fail summary. Not a standard.
MAX_IMPOSSIBLE_FRAC <- 0.05

# Genome sizes (bp), keyed by species name or genus, for coverage maths.
GENOME_SIZES <- c(
  `Escherichia coli` = 5.0e6, `Bacteroides fragilis` = 5.2e6,
  `Faecalibacterium prausnitzii` = 3.1e6, `Fusobacterium nucleatum` = 2.4e6,
  `Cutibacterium acnes` = 2.5e6, `Klebsiella pneumoniae` = 5.5e6,
  Escherichia = 5.0e6, Shigella = 4.6e6, Klebsiella = 5.5e6, Salmonella = 4.8e6,
  Bacteroides = 5.5e6, Parabacteroides = 6.2e6, Prevotella = 3.5e6,
  Faecalibacterium = 3.1e6, Roseburia = 3.9e6, Eubacterium = 3.5e6,
  Blautia = 6.0e6, Ruminococcus = 3.5e6, Bifidobacterium = 2.3e6,
  Lactobacillus = 2.2e6, Enterococcus = 3.0e6, Clostridium = 4.0e6,
  Akkermansia = 2.7e6, Fusobacterium = 2.4e6, Streptococcus = 2.1e6,
  Staphylococcus = 2.8e6, Pseudomonas = 6.3e6, Cutibacterium = 2.5e6,
  Ralstonia = 5.5e6, Bradyrhizobium = 8.5e6, Sphingomonas = 4.0e6,
  Stutzerimonas = 4.7e6, Natronomonas = 2.8e6, Arthrobacter = 4.5e6,
  Elizabethkingia = 4.1e6, Paenibacillus = 6.0e6
)
DEFAULT_GENOME <- 4.0e6

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. SETUP
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
if (length(args) >= 1) INPUT_FILE <- args[1]
if (length(args) >= 2) OUTDIR     <- args[2]

if (!file.exists(ANNOT_FILE))
  stop("taxon_annotation.R not found at '", ANNOT_FILE, "'.")
source(ANNOT_FILE)
test_annotation()
gut_cat <- if (!is.null(GUT_CATALOGUE)) load_gut_catalogue(GUT_CATALOGUE) else NULL

dir.create(OUTDIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
wr <- function(x, f) utils::write.table(
  x, file.path(OUTDIR, f), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

verdict <- character(0)
say <- function(...) { msg <- paste0(...); verdict <<- c(verdict, msg); cat(msg, "\n") }

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. LOAD, PARSE, ANNOTATE
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

raw <- utils::read.delim(INPUT_FILE, sep = "\t", header = TRUE,
                         check.names = FALSE, comment.char = "#",
                         stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(raw)[1] <- "clade_name"

# load in crypts
crypts <- read.csv(CRYPT_FILE)%>%
  pull(sample)

raw <- raw[,colnames(raw)%in%c('clade_name',crypts)]

# drop non-sample columns (e.g. NCBI_tax_id, which is pipe-separated text)
num_ok <- vapply(raw[-1], function(x)
  is.numeric(x) || !any(is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x)))), logical(1))
raw <- raw[, c(TRUE, num_ok), drop = FALSE]
for (j in 2:ncol(raw)) raw[[j]] <- as.numeric(raw[[j]])

# MetaPhlAn/Bracken lineage tables are NESTED: the phylum row already contains
# its genera. Taking all rows double-counts. Select exactly one rank.
last_tok  <- sub(".*\\|", "", raw$clade_name)
rank_code <- sub("__.*", "", last_tok)
taxon     <- sub("^[a-z]__", "", last_tok)

is_total <- rank_code == "d" & !grepl("\\|", raw$clade_name)
total_classified <- if (any(is_total)) colSums(raw[is_total, -1, drop = FALSE]) else NULL

## --- how much signal exists at each rank? ---------------------------------
rank_lbl <- c(d = "domain", p = "phylum", c = "class", o = "order",
              f = "family", g = "genus", s = "species", t = "SGB")
rank_rep <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(rank_lbl), function(rk) {
  sel <- rank_code == rk
  if (!any(sel)) return(NULL)
  m <- as.matrix(raw[sel, -1, drop = FALSE]); m[is.na(m)] <- 0
  data.frame(rank = rank_lbl[[rk]], code = rk, n_rows = sum(sel),
             total_reads = sum(m),
             median_reads_per_sample = stats::median(colSums(m)),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
if (!is.null(rank_rep)) { print(rank_rep); wr(rank_rep, "00_rank_availability.tsv") }

keep <- rank_code == RANK
if (!any(keep)) stop("No rows at rank '", RANK, "'. Present: ",
                     paste(unique(rank_code), collapse = ", "))

mat <- as.matrix(raw[keep, -1, drop = FALSE])
rownames(mat) <- taxon[keep]
lineage_all <- raw$clade_name[keep]
mat[is.na(mat)] <- 0
mat <- round(mat)
nz  <- rowSums(mat) > 0
mat <- mat[nz, , drop = FALSE]; lineage_all <- lineage_all[nz]

empty <- colSums(mat) == 0
if (any(empty)) {
  message("Dropping ", sum(empty), " sample(s) with 0 classified reads.")
  if (!is.null(total_classified)) total_classified <- total_classified[!empty]
  mat <- mat[, !empty, drop = FALSE]
}

samples  <- colnames(mat)
n_sample <- length(samples)
libsize  <- colSums(mat)
if (is.null(total_classified)) total_classified <- libsize

cat(sprintf("\nLoaded %d taxa at rank '%s' across %d samples.\n\n",
            nrow(mat), RANK, n_sample))

ann <- annotate_taxa(rownames(mat),
                     rank = if (RANK %in% c("s", "t")) "s" else "g",
                     gut_catalogue = gut_cat, lineage = lineage_all)
stopifnot(identical(ann$taxon, rownames(mat)))
annotation_report(ann, mat)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. PER-SAMPLE DEPTH
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

depth <- data.frame(
  sample              = samples,
  classified_reads    = as.integer(libsize),
  total_all_ranks     = as.integer(total_classified[samples]),
  n_taxa_detected     = colSums(mat >= MIN_READS_TAXON),
  top_taxon           = rownames(mat)[apply(mat, 2, which.max)],
  top_taxon_frac      = round(apply(mat, 2, max) / pmax(libsize, 1), 3),
  min_detectable_relab = signif(MIN_READS_TAXON / pmax(libsize, 1), 3),
  stringsAsFactors    = FALSE
)
depth <- depth[order(depth$classified_reads), ]
wr(depth, "01_depth_per_sample.tsv")

say("=== DEPTH ===")
say(sprintf("Classified reads/sample: median %s, range %s - %s",
            format(median(libsize), big.mark = ","),
            format(min(libsize), big.mark = ","),
            format(max(libsize), big.mark = ",")))
say(sprintf("At median depth nothing below ~%.2g relative abundance is visible.",
            MIN_READS_TAXON / median(libsize)))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. GENOME-EQUIVALENT COVERAGE AND THE THREE THRESHOLDS
##
##  T_DETECT   presence/absence only. A few reads says "seen", nothing more.
##
##  T_BREADTH  coverage at which a call can be VERIFIED by checking reads
##             spread across the genome rather than piling onto conserved or
##             repetitive regions. Below it, a real low-abundance organism and
##             a misassignment artefact look identical.
##
##  T_QUANT    reads needed to COMPARE abundance between samples. Counts carry
##             Poisson shot noise, so log(k) has SE ~ 1/sqrt(k) and
##             SE(log ratio) = sqrt(1/k1 + 1/k2). To resolve a fold-change F at
##             power (1-beta), two-sided alpha:
##
##                k >= 2 * ((z_{1-alpha/2} + z_{1-beta}) / log(F))^2
##
##             ~33 reads for 2-fold, ~96 for 1.5-fold, ~315 for 1.25-fold.
##             This is a FLOOR: it assumes pure Poisson sampling with no
##             overdispersion, whereas real microbiome counts have
##             Var = mu + phi*mu^2 with phi ~ 0.5-2. Crucially, a taxon below
##             T_QUANT cannot support an abundance comparison at ANY sample
##             size, because the limit is per-sample shot noise, not n.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

gsize <- unname(GENOME_SIZES[ann$name])
alt   <- unname(GENOME_SIZES[ann$genus])
gsize[is.na(gsize)] <- alt[is.na(gsize)]
gsize[is.na(gsize)] <- DEFAULT_GENOME
bases_per_read <- READ_LEN * (if (PAIRED) 2 else 1)

cov_mat <- sweep(mat * bases_per_read, 1, gsize, "/")   # taxa x samples, in X
max_cov_overall <- max(cov_mat)

reads_for_fold <- function(fold, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80) {
  z <- stats::qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) + stats::qnorm(power)
  ceiling(2 * (z / log(fold))^2)
}
T_DETECT    <- MIN_READS_TAXON
T_BREADTH_X <- 0.05
T_QUANT_2X  <- reads_for_fold(2.0)
T_QUANT_15X <- reads_for_fold(1.5)

## ALL of these are PER TAXON PER SAMPLE. They are never comparable to a
## sample's total read count summed over taxa -- that comparison is the single
## easiest way to conclude the data are adequate when they are not.

# reads equivalent of the breadth threshold, for a typical genome
T_BREADTH_READS <- ceiling(T_BREADTH_X * DEFAULT_GENOME / bases_per_read)

# The binding constraint. To use a taxon in a between-sample abundance
# comparison you need BOTH: enough coverage to verify the call is real
# (breadth), and enough reads to resolve the effect size (shot noise).
# Note breadth is by far the more demanding of the two -- confirming an
# organism is present is harder than quantifying it once you believe it.
T_USABLE_2X  <- max(T_BREADTH_READS, T_QUANT_2X)
T_USABLE_15X <- max(T_BREADTH_READS, T_QUANT_15X)

thresholds <- data.frame(
  threshold = c("T_DETECT", "T_QUANT_2fold", "T_QUANT_1.5fold", "T_BREADTH",
                "T_USABLE_2fold", "T_USABLE_1.5fold"),
  scope = "per taxon, per sample",
  basis = c("presence/absence only",
            "Poisson floor to resolve 2-fold difference, 80% power",
            "Poisson floor to resolve 1.5-fold difference, 80% power",
            "coverage at which breadth of genome covered can be checked",
            "breadth AND 2-fold resolution -- the binding constraint",
            "breadth AND 1.5-fold resolution -- the binding constraint"),
  reads_required = c(T_DETECT, T_QUANT_2X, T_QUANT_15X, T_BREADTH_READS,
                     T_USABLE_2X, T_USABLE_15X),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
thresholds$coverage_X_required <-
  signif(thresholds$reads_required * bases_per_read / DEFAULT_GENOME, 3)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. TAXON ANNOTATION + EVIDENCE  (FIGURE 1 data)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

relab <- sweep(mat, 2, pmax(libsize, 1), "/")

contam <- score_evidence(
  ann, mat,
  blanks = if (length(BLANKS)) intersect(BLANKS, samples) else NULL,
  read_len = READ_LEN, paired = PAIRED, genome_sizes = GENOME_SIZES,
  min_reads = MIN_READS_TAXON, default_genome = DEFAULT_GENOME
)
contam$total_reads <- rowSums(mat)
contam$mean_relab  <- signif(rowMeans(relab), 3)

# One provenance label per taxon, shared by all three figures so the colour
# scale matches. Levels are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE and exhaustive, so they sum to
# the library size and can be stacked directly.
#
# "impossible_clade" is split out from "contaminant" deliberately. Both are
# non-biological, but they carry different evidential weight: a blacklist call
# can be argued with on grounds of list curation, whereas a halophilic
# archaeon in a colonic crypt cannot. Keeping them separate lets a figure show
# the conservative number and the unarguable one side by side.
prov <- rep("unclassified", nrow(mat))
prov[ann$allowlist_status == "unnamed_sgb"]   <- "unnamed_sgb"
prov[ann$allowlist_status == "oral"]          <- "oral"
prov[ann$allowlist_status == "gut"]           <- "gut"
prov[ann$allowlist_status == "environmental"] <- "contaminant"
prov[ann$blacklist_status == "contaminant"]   <- "contaminant"
prov[ann$env_clade]                           <- "impossible_clade"  # overrides
PROV_LEVELS <- c("contaminant", "impossible_clade", "gut", "oral",
                 "unclassified", "unnamed_sgb")
prov <- factor(prov, levels = PROV_LEVELS)

contam$provenance <- prov[match(contam$taxon, rownames(mat))]
contam <- contam[order(-contam$total_reads), ]

frac_impossible   <- sum(mat[prov == "impossible_clade", , drop = FALSE]) / sum(mat)
frac_blacklisted  <- sum(mat[prov == "contaminant", , drop = FALSE]) / sum(mat)
# combined non-biological load -- this is the headline "% contaminant" figure
frac_contam_reads <- frac_blacklisted + frac_impossible
frac_gut_reads    <- sum(mat[prov == "gut", , drop = FALSE]) / sum(mat)
frac_env_clade    <- frac_impossible

## --- internal false-positive control --------------------------------------
## Reads assigned to clades that cannot occur in a human colon (halophilic
## archaea, soil Acidobacteria, Cyanobacteria). Their true abundance is zero,
## so every such read is a classifier error or a contaminant. This is the
## closest thing to a built-in negative control a taxonomic profile offers,
## and it bounds how much of the rest of the table to believe. It is also a
## stronger argument than the blacklist, because it cannot be disputed on
## grounds of list curation.
worst <- head(order(-rowSums(mat) * ann$env_clade), 20)
## --- decoy-based FDR: what abundance must a taxon exceed to be believed? ---
## Impossible clades are decoys. For a per-taxon abundance threshold x:
##   D(x) = decoy taxa above x
##   T(x) = target taxa above x
##   expected false targets above x = D(x) * (N_target_DB / N_decoy_DB)
##   FDR(x) = expected false targets / T(x)
## The threshold at which FDR falls below FDR_TARGET is a DERIVED detection
## limit, calibrated on your own data, rather than a convention.
decoy_v  <- prov == "impossible_clade"
taxon_ab <- rowMeans(relab)                     # mean relative abundance

if (is.na(DB_N_DECOY) || is.na(DB_N_TARGET)) {
  db_scale <- sum(!decoy_v) / max(sum(decoy_v), 1)

} else {
}

grid <- sort(unique(c(0, stats::quantile(taxon_ab[taxon_ab > 0],
                                         probs = seq(0, 1, 0.01), na.rm = TRUE))))
fdr_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(grid, function(x) {
  D <- sum(taxon_ab >= x & decoy_v)
  T_ <- sum(taxon_ab >= x & !decoy_v)
  data.frame(relab_threshold = signif(x, 3),
             reads_at_median_depth = ceiling(x * stats::median(libsize)),
             n_decoy_taxa = D, n_target_taxa = T_,
             est_false_targets = round(D * db_scale, 1),
             FDR = if (T_ > 0) signif(min(1, D * db_scale / T_), 3) else NA_real_,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

ok_idx <- which(!is.na(fdr_tab$FDR) & fdr_tab$FDR <= FDR_TARGET)
say("")
say("=== DECOY-BASED DETECTION THRESHOLD ===")
say(sprintf("Decoy scaling factor (target:decoy in database) = %.1f", db_scale))
if (length(ok_idx)) {
  r <- fdr_tab[min(ok_idx), ]
  say(sprintf("FDR falls below %.0f%% only above mean relative abundance %.3g",
              100 * FDR_TARGET, r$relab_threshold))
  say(sprintf("  = ~%s reads at median library size; %d taxa clear it.",
              format(r$reads_at_median_depth, big.mark = ","), r$n_target_taxa))
  say("  Anything below this cannot be distinguished from misassignment noise.")
} else {
  say(sprintf("FDR NEVER falls below %.0f%% at any abundance threshold.",
              100 * FDR_TARGET))
  say("  -> Decoy taxa are as abundant as real ones. No taxon in this table")
  say("     can be separated from misassignment noise on abundance alone.")
}

## --- possible blanks among your columns -----------------------------------
blank_like <- grepl("blank|ntc|neg|ctrl|control|water|h2o|empty", samples, ignore.case = TRUE)
cand <- data.frame(sample = samples, classified_reads = as.integer(libsize),
                   name_looks_like_blank = blank_like,
                   in_lowest_5pct_depth = libsize <= quantile(libsize, 0.05),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cand <- cand[cand$name_looks_like_blank | cand$in_lowest_5pct_depth, ]

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. FIGURE 2 data: per-sample composition
##    Shows contamination is systemic, not a few bad libraries. The MINIMUM
##    contaminant fraction across samples is the number that makes the point.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fig2 <- data.frame(sample = samples, total_reads = as.integer(libsize),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
for (p in PROV_LEVELS) {
  r <- colSums(mat[prov == p, , drop = FALSE])
  fig2[[paste0("reads_", p)]] <- as.integer(r)
  fig2[[paste0("relab_", p)]] <- round(r / pmax(libsize, 1), 5)
}
# combined non-biological load: blacklisted contaminants PLUS impossible
# clades. Use this for the figure 2 scatter against relab_gut; the two
# components remain available separately for a stacked bar.
fig2$reads_nonbiological <- fig2$reads_contaminant + fig2$reads_impossible_clade
fig2$relab_nonbiological <- round(fig2$relab_contaminant + fig2$relab_impossible_clade, 5)

fig2$n_taxa_gut_detected        <- colSums(mat[prov == "gut", , drop = FALSE] >= T_DETECT)
fig2$n_taxa_impossible_detected <- colSums(mat[prov == "impossible_clade", , drop = FALSE] >= T_DETECT)
fig2$top_taxon       <- rownames(mat)[apply(mat, 2, which.max)]
fig2$top_taxon_prov  <- as.character(prov[apply(mat, 2, which.max)])
fig2$top_taxon_relab <- round(apply(mat, 2, max) / pmax(libsize, 1), 4)
fig2 <- fig2[order(-fig2$relab_nonbiological), ]
wr(fig2, "fig2_sample_composition_wide.tsv")

fig2_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(PROV_LEVELS, function(p) {
  r <- colSums(mat[prov == p, , drop = FALSE])
  data.frame(sample = samples, provenance = p, reads = as.integer(r),
             relab = round(r / pmax(libsize, 1), 5), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
wr(fig2_long, "fig2_sample_composition_long.tsv")

say("")
say("=== FIGURE 2: is contamination systemic? ===")
say(sprintf("Non-biological relative abundance per sample: median %.1f%%, IQR %.1f-%.1f%%, MIN %.1f%%",
            100 * median(fig2$relab_nonbiological),
            100 * quantile(fig2$relab_nonbiological, 0.25),
            100 * quantile(fig2$relab_nonbiological, 0.75),
            100 * min(fig2$relab_nonbiological)))
say(sprintf("%d/%d samples (%.0f%%) are >50%% non-biological; %d (%.0f%%) are >90%%.",
            sum(fig2$relab_nonbiological > 0.5), nrow(fig2),
            100 * mean(fig2$relab_nonbiological > 0.5),
            sum(fig2$relab_nonbiological > 0.9),
            100 * mean(fig2$relab_nonbiological > 0.9)))
say(sprintf("Impossible-clade fraction alone: median %.1f%%, MIN %.1f%%, present in %d/%d samples.",
            100 * median(fig2$relab_impossible_clade),
            100 * min(fig2$relab_impossible_clade),
            sum(fig2$reads_impossible_clade > 0), nrow(fig2)))
say("  -> A high MINIMUM across samples means this is a property of the")
say("     protocol (low input + 10-12 PCR cycles), not of outlier libraries.")
say("  -> The impossible-clade column is the unarguable version of the same")
say("     point: those reads have a true abundance of zero in every sample.")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. FIGURE 3 data: per-sample gut coverage against the thresholds
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

gut_i <- which(prov == "gut")
gmat <- mat[gut_i, , drop = FALSE]
gcov <- cov_mat[gut_i, , drop = FALSE]
pos  <- function(x) if (any(x > 0)) x[x > 0] else NA_real_

fig3 <- data.frame(
  sample      = samples,
  total_reads = as.integer(libsize),
  gut_reads   = as.integer(colSums(gmat)),
  gut_relab   = round(colSums(gmat) / pmax(libsize, 1), 5),
  # summed genome equivalents: an upper bound on gut-derived DNA present
  gut_genome_equivalents = signif(colSums(gcov), 3),
  # the honest per-organism number -- summing across taxa overstates what
  # you can actually do with any single one of them
  max_gut_coverage_X    = signif(apply(gcov, 2, max), 3),
  median_gut_coverage_X = signif(apply(gcov, 2, function(x) stats::median(pos(x))), 3),
  # counts of INDIVIDUAL gut taxa clearing each per-taxon bar in this sample.
  # These, not the sample's total gut reads, are what determine whether an
  # abundance comparison is possible.
  n_gut_detected           = colSums(gmat >= T_DETECT),
  n_gut_quantifiable_2x    = colSums(gmat >= T_QUANT_2X),
  n_gut_quantifiable_15x   = colSums(gmat >= T_QUANT_15X),
  n_gut_breadth_verifiable = colSums(gcov >= T_BREADTH_X),
  # both conditions at once -- the number that actually matters
  n_gut_usable_2x          = colSums(gmat >= T_USABLE_2X),
  n_gut_usable_15x         = colSums(gmat >= T_USABLE_15X),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
fig3 <- fig3[order(-fig3$gut_reads), ]
  


```

```{r}
pcol <- c(contaminant = "firebrick", gut = "darkslateblue", oral = "goldenrod",
          unclassified = "grey60", unnamed_sgb = "grey80")

fig1_scatter<-ggplot(data=contam, aes(x=total_reads,y=mean_relab,col=provenance))+
  geom_point()+
  
  scale_color_manual(values=pcol,
                    breaks=c('contaminant','gut','oral','unclassified','unnamed_sgb'),
                     labels=c('Contaminant','Oral Bacteria','Gut Bacteria',
                               'Unclassified','Unnamed_SGB'))+
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10()+
  theme_classic()+
  labs(x='Total read across samples',y='Mean relative abundance across samples',
       col='Species Classification')+
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size=20,face='bold'),
        axis.text = element_text(size=16,face='bold'),
        legend.position='bottom',
        legend.title = element_text(size=20,face='bold'),
        legend.text = element_text(size=16,face='bold')
        )

top10_rel_ab<-contam%>%arrange(desc(mean_relab))%>%head(20)
fig1_bar<-ggplot(data=top10_rel_ab, aes(x=mean_relab,y=fct_reorder(species,mean_relab),fill=provenance))+
  geom_bar(stat='identity')+
  scale_fill_manual(values=pcol,
                    breaks=c('contaminant','gut','oral','unclassified','unnamed_sgb'),
                     labels=c('Contaminant','Oral Bacteria','Gut Bacteria',
                               'Unclassified','Unnamed_SGB'))+
  labs(y='',fill='',x='Mean relative abundance\nacross samples')+
  scale_x_continuous(labels=label_percent())+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size=20,face='bold'),
        axis.text = element_text(size=16,face='bold'),
        legend.position='none',
        legend.title = element_text(size=20,face='bold'),
        legend.text = element_text(size=16,face='bold')
        )


supp_fig10a_combined<-fig1_scatter+fig1_bar+plot_layout(widths = c(3, 1))
ggsave('./supp_fig10a_mean_read_abundance_all_bacteria.png',supp_fig10a_combined,width=18,height=10,dpi=200)
```

plot figure 2 : relative reads verus relative abundance

```{r}
prop_nonbiological_enriched=round(nrow(fig2[fig2$relab_nonbiological>0.5,])/nrow(fig2),2)*100

contaminant_gut_relab_plt<-ggplot(data=fig2,aes(x=relab_gut,y=relab_nonbiological ,col='grey30'))+
  geom_point(col='grey30')+
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1))+
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,1))+
  labs(x="Combined relative abundance of gut taxa per sample",
       y="Combined relative abundance of contaminant taxa per sample")+
  geom_hline(yintercept=0.5,linewidth=1,linetype=5,col='grey30')+
  geom_text(label=paste0('Contaminant taxa > 50% of reads\n[',prop_nonbiological_enriched,'% of samples]'), ,x=Inf,hjust=1,vjust=0.50,y=0.5,
            col='black',size=6,col='black')+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size=20,face='bold'),
        axis.text = element_text(size=16,face='bold'),
        legend.position='none',
        legend.title = element_text(size=20,face='bold'),
        legend.text = element_text(size=16,face='bold')
        )

impossible_gut_relab_plt<-ggplot(data=fig2,aes(x=relab_gut,y=relab_impossible_clade,col='grey30'))+
  geom_point(col='grey30')+
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1))+
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,1))+
  labs(x='Combined relative abundance of gut taxa per sample',
       y="Combined relative abundance of 'impossible taxa' per sample")+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size=20,face='bold'),
        axis.text = element_text(size=16,face='bold'),
        legend.position='none',
        legend.title = element_text(size=20,face='bold'),
        legend.text = element_text(size=16,face='bold')
        )

supp_fig10b_combined=contaminant_gut_relab_plt|impossible_gut_relab_plt
ggsave('./supp_fig10b_relab_nonbio_impossible.png',supp_fig10b_combined,width=18,height=10,dpi=200)
```

```{r}
cov_of <- function(reads) reads * bases_per_read / DEFAULT_GENOME

coverage_plt<-ggplot(data=fig3,aes(x=gut_reads+1,y=max_gut_coverage_X+1e-9))+
  scale_x_log10()+
  scale_y_log10()+
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0.0001,50))+
  labs(x='Total gut taxa reads per sample',
       y='Coverage of best single gut taxon [X]')+
  geom_point(col='grey10')+
  geom_hline(yintercept=cov_of(T_DETECT),col="grey50",linetype=5)+
  geom_text(label='Bacteria detectable [min 10 reads]',x=Inf,vjust=-0.5,hjust=1.02,size=5,y=log10(cov_of(T_DETECT)),col="grey50",inherit.aes = FALSE)+
  
  geom_hline(yintercept=cov_of(T_QUANT_2X),  col = "steelblue", linetype = 2)+
  geom_text(label='Detect 2-fold change [min 33 reads]',x=Inf,vjust=-0.5,hjust=1.02,size=5,y=log10(cov_of(T_QUANT_2X)),col="steelblue")+
  geom_hline(yintercept=T_BREADTH_X,  col = "firebrick", linetype = 2)+
  geom_text(label='Genome breadth-verifiable\n[min 667 reads]',x=Inf,vjust=0.5,hjust=1.02,y=log10(T_BREADTH_X),size=5,col="firebrick")+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size=20,face='bold'),
        axis.text = element_text(size=16,face='bold'),
        legend.position='none',
        legend.title = element_text(size=20,face='bold'),
        legend.text = element_text(size=16,face='bold')
        )

summary_taxa_dataected<-rbind(
    detected      = table(factor(pmin(fig3$n_gut_detected, 5), levels = 0:5)),
    quant_2fold   = table(factor(pmin(fig3$n_gut_quantifiable_2x, 5), levels = 0:5)),
    usable_2fold  = table(factor(pmin(fig3$n_gut_usable_2x, 5), levels = 0:5))
  )%>%
  as.data.frame()%>%
  rownames_to_column(var='threshold')%>%
  
  pivot_longer(cols=!contains('threshold'))

detectable_plt<-ggplot(data=summary_taxa_dataected,aes(x=threshold,fill=name,y=value))+
  geom_bar(stat='identity',col='black')+
  labs(x='Fraction of samples',y='',fill='Number of\ngut taxa')+
  scale_x_discrete(breaks=c("detected","quant_2fold", "usable_2fold"),
                   labels=c('Detected','Detect 2-fold\nchange','Genome Breadth verify')
  )+
  scale_fill_manual(breaks=c(5,4,3,2,1,0),
                    labels=c('5+','4','3','2','1','0'),
                    values=c('grey0','grey20','grey40','grey60','grey80','grey100'))+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size=20,face='bold'),
        axis.text = element_text(size=16,face='bold'),
        legend.position='bottom',
        legend.title = element_text(size=20,face='bold'),
        legend.text = element_text(size=16,face='bold')
        )
supp_fig10c_combined<-coverage_plt|detectable_plt+plot_layout(width=c(10,1))
ggsave('./supp_fig10c_gut_taxa_coverage.png',supp_fig10c_combined,width=18,height=10,dpi=150)
```
